inspiration: repipe round 4 need binary-maze-pointer-becomes; sub_402020 walks a 585-byte packed maze at 0x403550 whose first row is zeroes, and both pointers into it printed = ""
decisions: The FILED hypothesis ('string rendering considers the first NUL without accounting for subsequent indexed reads') is OVERTURNED, exactly as the captain's in-tick refutation said, and its one-byte control is reproduced: poking 0x403550 from 00 to 0x41 turns the output into `v16 = "A"`, so stopping at the first NUL is not what loses the address.

The captain's replacement diagnosis -- the constant is `char *` because it shares a merged live range with a genuine `char *` parameter -- is UPHELD and deliberately NOT repaired. Re-typing a merged live range is P5/P6 work far outside this need's `scope: small`, and the printer is doing the right thing for a `char *` constant once that type exists. What is wrong is the printer's EVIDENCE test: `StringManager::isString` accepts a location on the strength of zero validated characters, because `checkCharacters` walks only to the first terminator.

The captain's warning that the naive fix is gameable turned out to understate it: suppressing every zero-character literal is WRONG, not merely cheap. A whole-corpus sweep found `setlocale(6,"")` plus five more genuine empty literals in the vendored coreutils fixtures alone (all one merged `""` at 0x7661 in regglobal_fmt_x86_64, stored as the tail NUL of "Report bugs to: %s\n"), and the naive rule turned every one of them into an address. That is what drove the byte-evidence half of the design.

A 16-byte all-printable-or-NUL window was the SECOND wrong design and was caught by the same sweep: it declined four more real empty literals (du 0x1aa00 and 0x1af20, pathchk 0x8aeb, ssh-keysign 0x836a6), each the head of a short string table whose window runs past the table's end into relocation bytes. The shipped rule judges only the FIRST run after the terminator, which is a falsification test -- it says no only where the bytes positively contradict string data -- so everything it cannot judge keeps the upstream literal.

The acceptance probe as filed was retargetable but its `expect` was not: `stdout_absent: = "";` plus `stdout_matches: 0x403550` says nothing about the real empty literal beside it. The promoted probe asserts BOTH directions on one function -- the blob keeps 0x402020 AND the genuine "" keeps its quotes -- so neither the naive rule nor the window rule could pass it.

The one red rust-test target is environmental, not this change: the assertion requires the C++ spelling `xunknown4` from an oracle binary that no longer exists, and the repipe launcher points KUNA_DECOMP_TEST at kuna's own decomp_test_dbg.
speed_method: scripts.pipeline.timeit (warmup + median over 9 repeats) on the fixture; hand-timed median over 9 runs on the dataset witness
speed_note: The fixture's -7.95% is inside the measured noise floor for a single small target; the witness (Sabloom Text 6.exe, sub_402020) is 0.18 s median in BOTH arms. The added work is one 16-byte load_fill per zero-character literal render, which is the only site the gate can reach.

sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, --option emptystrconst off vs default, over 58 images (decbench ELF corpus + RE-dataset PE/ELF crackmes); the ON arm re-run for every image whose OFF output contains a zero-character literal, which is the only site the gate can reach
sweep.note: every changed line is a 1:1 substitution of a `""` literal by `(type *)0xADDR`; no statement added, deleted, moved or re-anchored, and no file changed line count. Each declined address was read back: the maze, and a jump-table/relocation array at 0x10016 in libbsd.so.0.11.7 (00 00 28 63 ff ff f8 62). The 312 kept are the load-bearing number -- an earlier all-printable-window design declined 4 of them.

gates.make rust-test: 363 targets ok, 1 red: verify_w10_proto_unlock::w10_proto_unlock_const_return_collapses_no_tied_roundtrip, the known KUNA_DECOMP_TEST oracle artifact.
